title: Frontend asks for the CPH number as one nine-character box; Design release 1 asks for it as three boxes sized to the county, parish and holding parts

finding.frontend: The County Parish Holding page renders a single text input ten characters wide, hinted "For example, 123456789 or 123/456/789." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/template.njk:11-23, copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/copy/copy.en.js:3-6). A trader may type the number with or without slashes; the controller strips any slashes and then requires exactly nine digits (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:34-40,73-79). Nothing on the page tells the trader that the nine digits are two, then three, then four, and nothing stops them mistyping the split.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 asks for the same nine digits in three separate boxes under one legend, "CPH number", hinted "For example 12/345/6789" (app/views/partials/cph-number-input.html:4-59, included at app/views/cph-number.html:53). The boxes are two, three and four characters wide, each numeric-only and capped by `maxlength`, and each carries a label — County, Parish, Holding number — that is present for screen readers but hidden from sight, so on the page a trader meets three boxes whose widths and hint carry the format. The captured screenshot dr1-cph-number-details-open shows this: three unlabelled boxes of increasing width beneath the worked example.
finding.difference: Replace the single CPH input with a three-part input: county (2 digits), parish (3 digits), holding number (4 digits), numeric input mode, capped at their own lengths, under one legend and the hint "For example 12/345/6789". Keep the nine-digit rule as the combined validation. This changes the shape of one control on one page and needs no data change — the answer is still stored as `countyParishHoldingCph` and the existing controller already normalises a slashed value (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:75-77). The error messages will need re-pointing at the part that is wrong rather than at one box.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding more than one CPH input on the frontend page. The captured DOM of fe-cph-number holds exactly one, `countyParishHoldingCph`.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier: capture/html/frontend/fe-cph-number.html holds exactly one input, id and name countyParishHoldingCph, class govuk-input--width-10, wrapped in a label-as-h1, hinted "For example, 123456789 or 123/456/789.", with nothing else between the heading and the button group. Read capture/html/prototype/dr1-cph-number.html: three inputs named cphNumber-county, cphNumber-parish and cphNumber-holding at widths 2, 3 and 4, each inputmode="numeric" with a matching maxlength and pattern="[0-9]*", inside one role="group" fieldset legended "CPH number" and hinted "For example 12/345/6789". Checked the claim that the three part labels are hidden from sight rather than absent, because the DOM carries ordinary govuk-date-input__label elements and those normally render: opened evidence/prototype@491b3926/page/dr1-cph-number.png and the three boxes are genuinely unlabelled on screen, then found the reason at app/assets/sass/application.scss:2864-2874, where .app-cph-number-page__cph-input .govuk-date-input__label is clipped to a one-pixel box. The sentence is right and now has a citation behind it. Verified the frontend controller at the cited lines: the nine-digit rule is requiredExactDigits at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:34-40 and the slash strip at :77. CORRECT.
finding.correction: The claim stands and is if anything understated in two places, both of which I checked. First, the split changes what a trader reads back as well as what they type: Design release 1 stores and echoes the value slashed, so its Consignment addresses row reads "12/345/6789" and its review page reads the same (dr1-roles-and-addresses-answered, dr1-review-notification), while Frontend strips the slashes and echoes "123456789" on both (fe-addresses-hub-complete, fe-check-answers). Whoever builds this should settle the echoed format with the input, not after it. Second, the difference slot says to keep the nine-digit rule as the combined validation, and that is the right call, but it is Frontend's own rule and not a shared one: Design release 1 does not validate the CPH at all — validateCphNumber returns an empty error list unconditionally (app/routes.js:2840-2864) — so there is no requirement here to copy and nothing to reconcile. What the requirements side does state, and what the three boxes carry, is the shape of the number — two, then three, then four — which Frontend states nowhere.
